sources.entry: Pterodactyl - Management panel for game servers, with an intuitive UI for end users. (Source Code) MIT PHP
Pterodactyl | Game server management panel running each server in Docker

summary.one_liner: Pterodactyl Panel is a free, open-source web panel for managing game servers, with each server running in its own isolated Docker container.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Pterodactyl as a game server management panel built with PHP, React, and Go, which runs all game servers in isolated Docker containers and exposes a web UI to end users. It states that the v2.0.0-beta.1 release adds a modernized tech stack, a redesigned admin area, and an extension SDK built into the panel. Development happens on the 2.0-develop branch, while 1.0-develop is the current stable line. The README lists supported games including Minecraft (Paper, Sponge, Bungeecord, Waterfall), Rust, Terraria, TeamSpeak, Mumble, Team Fortress 2, Counter-Strike: Global Offensive, Garry's Mod, and ARK: Survival Evolved, plus community-provided games such as Factorio, Squad, and Xonotic. Documentation covers the panel and Wings (the server-side daemon), and community guides and Discord are linked for help.
use_cases: manage multiple game servers from one web panel
run game servers in isolated Docker containers
give customers a self-service UI for their game servers
host Rust, Terraria, or Counter-Strike servers
run Discord or Node.js/Python bots alongside game servers
notable: Runs each game server in an isolated Docker container
Web UI for end users alongside an admin area
v2 beta adds an extension SDK built into the panel
Large catalog of supported games via Docker images and community nests
Separate Wings daemon documented alongside the panel
caveats: v2 is in beta; 1.0-develop is the current stable line
Installation and setup steps are not included in the README; it points to external documentation
